clearedSpotChecks.check: Division branches of holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 that FullMath, SqrtPriceMath and UnsafeMath reach (15,000 vectors aimed at udivremKnuth add-back, the qhat correction, the qhat overflow and both udivrem2by1 adjustments, for DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, MULMOD with a modulus below 2^192 and ADDMOD with an overflowing sum), all matching on Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Elysium.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I built 420 vectors of my own with a different seed and without the research agent's transcription (cycles/034/arbitrum-family.verify/divcheck.py): 240 DIV, MOD, SDIV and SMOD of the form Q*d - eps over two and three limb divisors, 120 MULMOD with T = k*m - small over a modulus below 2^192, and 60 ADDMOD with an overflowing sum. I ran them by eth_call against a state-override contract and compared each word with Python integers. Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain answered all 420 with no mismatch. Elysium answered 393 (27 rate-limit errors) with no mismatch (divcheck.json, divcheck_99901.json). Nitro master go.mod still pins github.com/holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 (line 39), and OffchainLabs/go-ethereum master core/vm/instructions.go is byte identical to the cycle 32 and cycle 34 copies. These are the shapes of FullMath.sol:47-49 and SqrtPriceMath.sol:209. The research file's raw/knuth132.json records 0 mismatches on 15,000 per chain and raw/plant.json shows a broken transcription would fail 4,190, so the set can fail.

clearedSpotChecks.check: EIP-2935 history contract 0x0000f908...2935 and ArbOS sender 0x...a4b05 called from the PoolManager address with empty calldata, empty calldata with value 1, transfer(address,uint256) and balanceOf(PoolManager): all revert with empty data, so a take or sync naming either address reverts only the caller's action.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I repeated the calls with from set to the PoolManager on all three chains at latest (Arbitrum One block 528,061,811, Robinhood Chain 124,397,434, Elysium 11,688,834; cycles/034/arbitrum-family.verify/special.json). The history contract has 133 bytes of code and 0xa4b05 has 1 byte. All 4 shapes revert with data 0x on both addresses. I added a fifth shape, a bare 32-byte word. The history contract answers it with a block hash, which is its specified get path. No PoolManager call produces 32-byte calldata to a currency or recipient: Currency.transfer sends 68 bytes or empty calldata (src/types/Currency.sol:48, 60-73), balanceOfSelf calls balanceOf with 36 bytes (src/types/Currency.sol:94), and sync and take revert when those calls revert (src/PoolManager.sol:285, 295; Currency.sol:51-52, 82-85). A pool whose currency is the history contract cannot be synced or settled, and victims would have to pick that pool themselves.

clearedSpotChecks.check: getNativeTokenManagementFrom() returns 0 on all three chains, so ArbNativeTokenManager minting and burning is off, and enabling it needs the chain owner.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I called ArbOwnerPublic 0x6b selector 0x3fecbab0 at latest on all three RPC URLs and got 0 each time; getScheduledUpgrade() (0x81ef944c) returned zeros (cycles/034/arbitrum-family.verify/arbos.txt). In Nitro master, ArbOwner.AddNativeTokenOwner refuses while the enabled time is 0 or in the future (precompiles/ArbOwner.go:142-149), and SetNativeTokenManagementFrom is an ArbOwner method, which only the chain owner can call. Mint and burn in precompiles/ArbNativeTokenManager.go act only on the caller's own balance and need native token owner membership (hasAccess). Even with the feature on, the burn cannot reach the PoolManager's balance. The actor for any hazard here is governance.
